svg.text: Rear-wheel drive Ackermann · 2 drive motors + 1 steering servo · every load returns to the (−) WAGO bus · all fuses inline · harness wire 18 AWG · carrier boards A, B, C shown
4 of 5: battery, motor module, UBEC (with both switch LEDs), Bauer · one spare (MEC-16)
Why the main fuse comes first:
it protects the battery-to-bus cable, which
sits upstream of every other fuse and so
cannot be protected by any of them. It also
covers the short bus → SW1 → split run.
7.5 A main · 5 A on each power-train load = 1.5×
lit only when SW1 is on
⚠ VM in: 2-pin 2.5 mm, ~3 A - needs an adapter
lit only when SW2 is on
5 V via carrier B to E5V
M1 + M3, both on the rear edge
real-time + BMS · FDCAN2: PB12 RX · PB13 TX · I²C1 PB6 SCL / PB7 SDA · PA15 PWM
ST-LINK V3EC with VCP · 5 V in on E5V, JP5 [5-6] · AFs per DS14539 Rev 3
C2 470 µF across the servo header
twisted pair · 120 Ω at each end, nowhere else
J7 2×5 header: pin 8 CAN_H · 10 CAN_L · 6 GND
read JP1 and the resistors before adding a 120 Ω
J7 pins 7 / 9: I²C1 SCL / SDA · J1: 5 V in (board C)
to the PC USB-CAN adapter, F-F cable · a stub
electronic differential across the two rear wheels is firmware;
the axle is not a diff. The motor-module I²C shares the INA226 bus.
Build order: verify 5 V on a meter → fuse → battery last.
Unknowns: SM-2P connector temperature under load · FRDM loaded current · servo stall current.
Switches: same 22 mm part, red = power train, green = logic. Each LED is wired from the switched side, so it lights only when its switch is on. Relay deferred (HW-12).
